k: There is a city on the glass.
src: 'There is a city on the glass.'

k: Where? I see sand. And more sand. And— is that a cactus, or a very still man?
src: 'Where? I see sand. And more sand. And— is that a cactus, or a very still man?'

k: White towers. Bells. Flags for a festival. Everyone is laughing. It is afternoon there.
src: 'White towers. Bells. Flags for a festival. Everyone is laughing. It is afternoon there.'

k: It is _always_ afternoon there.
src: 'It is _always_ afternoon there.'

k: Sable? Have you seen it before?
src: 'Sable? Have you seen it before?'

k: ...In the water. Before you found me. I think I was walking toward it.
src: '...In the water. Before you found me. I think I was walking toward it.'

k: I do not want to walk toward it anymore.
src: 'I do not want to walk toward it anymore.'

k: Sable saw a white city on the glass where it is always afternoon. She said she used to be walking toward it. She said she doesn't want to anymore.
src: 'Sable saw a white city on the glass where it is always afternoon. She said she used to be walking toward it. She said she doesn\'t want to anymore.'

k: A skull the size of a fishing boat, bleached and polished by the wind. Its eye sockets are full of sand.
src: 'A skull the size of a fishing boat, bleached and polished by the wind. Its eye sockets are full of sand.'

k: Bet I could fit in its mouth.
src: 'Bet I could fit in its mouth.'

k: Please don't test that.
src: 'Please don\'t test that.'

k: Bet I could fit in its mouth _twice_.
src: 'Bet I could fit in its mouth _twice_.'

k: Water, clear as glass, in the middle of all that sand. It doesn't look real. It is.
src: 'Water, clear as glass, in the middle of all that sand. It doesn\'t look real. It is.'

k: It is warm on top and cold underneath. It has layers.
src: 'It is warm on top and cold underneath. It has layers.'

k: Like bread.
src: 'Like bread.'

k: Keep walking, young ones. Or don't.
src: 'Keep walking, young ones. Or don\'t.'

k: Either one is a choice. That's the only thing the desert ever taught me.
src: 'Either one is a choice. That\'s the only thing the desert ever taught me.'

k: Visitors! Sit, sit. The palms don't mind.
src: 'Visitors! Sit, sit. The palms don\'t mind.'

k: Thirty years I've lived by this water. Do you know what a desert is for?
src: 'Thirty years I\'ve lived by this water. Do you know what a desert is for?'

k: Being... hot?
src: 'Being... hot?'

k: Wanting things. Out there, every mirage is the thing you want most. Then you decide whether to keep walking toward it.
src: 'Wanting things. Out there, every mirage is the thing you want most. Then you decide whether to keep walking toward it.'

k: "Have you ever seen one?"
src: '"Have you ever seen one?"'

k: "That sounds lonely."
src: '"That sounds lonely."'

k: Every morning. A girl in a blue dress, at a well in Aurenne. I was going to ask her to dance.
src: 'Every morning. A girl in a blue dress, at a well in Aurenne. I was going to ask her to dance.'

k: I came out here to make enough money to deserve her. She married a baker. Forty years ago.
src: 'I came out here to make enough money to deserve her. She married a baker. Forty years ago.'

k: Still. I see her every morning, at her well, laughing at something. I've decided it's a nice way to start the day.
src: 'Still. I see her every morning, at her well, laughing at something. I\'ve decided it\'s a nice way to start the day.'

k: Lonely? Child, I have palms, a pond, and the finest view of nothing in all Solmere.
src: 'Lonely? Child, I have palms, a pond, and the finest view of nothing in all Solmere.'

k: ...Yes. Yes, it is. Thank you for noticing. Nobody notices.
src: '...Yes. Yes, it is. Thank you for noticing. Nobody notices.'

k: Here. Glass-cutter's goggles. They won't stop the mirages, but they stop the glare. The mirages, you have to stop yourself.
src: 'Here. Glass-cutter\'s goggles. They won\'t stop the mirages, but they stop the glare. The mirages, you have to stop yourself.'

k: Move along, glass-walkers. This is Sarn's water. Sarn's sand. Sarn's shade.
src: 'Move along, glass-walkers. This is Sarn\'s water. Sarn\'s sand. Sarn\'s shade.'

k: Sarn's very possessive.
src: 'Sarn\'s very possessive.'

k: Sarn's very _stabby_.
src: 'Sarn\'s very _stabby_.'

k: ...Wait. You're Idris's dogs. SARN! WE GOT COMPANY!
src: '...Wait. You\'re Idris\'s dogs. SARN! WE GOT COMPANY!'

k: Ha! Pilgrims! Got water? Got gold? Got a pretty sword?
src: 'Ha! Pilgrims! Got water? Got gold? Got a pretty sword?'

k: No? Then you've got nothing I want. Walk on, little lambs. Walk on before I change my mind.
src: 'No? Then you\'ve got nothing I want. Walk on, little lambs. Walk on before I change my mind.'

k: Idris sent _children_? I'm insulted. I'm going to take your boots _and_ your dignity.
src: 'Idris sent _children_? I\'m insulted. I\'m going to take your boots _and_ your dignity.'

k: Funny. That's exactly what my last landlady said.
src: 'Funny. That\'s exactly what my last landlady said.'

k: Sarn the Jackal staggers, spits sand, and bolts for the deep dunes, howling about revenge. His crew scatters after him like startled birds.
src: 'Sarn the Jackal staggers, spits sand, and bolts for the deep dunes, howling about revenge. His crew scatters after him like startled birds.'

k: And STAY OUT of... wherever this is!
src: 'And STAY OUT of... wherever this is!'

k: We ran Sarn the Jackal out of his camp. Captain Idris owes us a purse.
src: 'We ran Sarn the Jackal out of his camp. Captain Idris owes us a purse.'

k: An airship lies nose-down in the dune like a beached whale. Smoke curls from her engine housing. Her name is painted on the bow in flaking gold: HALCYON.
src: 'An airship lies nose-down in the dune like a beached whale. Smoke curls from her engine housing. Her name is painted on the bow in flaking gold: HALCYON.'

k: Not the ship! Anything but the ship!
src: 'Not the ship! Anything but the ship!'

k: Between them and the ship, the sand bulges — and something vast and pale turns over beneath it, like a fish under ice.
src: 'Between them and the ship, the sand bulges — and something vast and pale turns over beneath it, like a fish under ice.'

k: Eat the cargo! Eat the— no, not the cargo either, that's _paid for_—
src: 'Eat the cargo! Eat the— no, not the cargo either, that\'s _paid for_—'

k: Hey! Up there! Are you all right?
src: 'Hey! Up there! Are you all right?'

k: Civilians! Wonderful! Run away, quickly, it's very hungry!
src: 'Civilians! Wonderful! Run away, quickly, it\'s very hungry!'

k: We're here to help!
src: 'We\'re here to help!'

k: Then help by being slower than me!
src: 'Then help by being slower than me!'

k: Sable — keep Pip back!
src: 'Sable — keep Pip back!'

k: Oi! I can fight!
src: 'Oi! I can fight!'

k: You cannot. You have no light yet. I will stand with you.
src: 'You cannot. You have no light yet. I will stand with you.'

k: ...Fine. But I'm _watching_. Aggressively.
src: '...Fine. But I\'m _watching_. Aggressively.'

k: The dune splits open, and Sandmaw rises out of it, shedding sand like water.
src: 'The dune splits open, and Sandmaw rises out of it, shedding sand like water.'

k: Sandmaw shudders, sinks, and is gone — leaving only a long ripple in the dune, slowly smoothing itself away.
src: 'Sandmaw shudders, sinks, and is gone — leaving only a long ripple in the dune, slowly smoothing itself away.'

k: Well! That was terrifying. I was magnificent. Did you see me being magnificent?
src: 'Well! That was terrifying. I was magnificent. Did you see me being magnificent?'

k: You hid behind Bram.
src: 'You hid behind Bram.'

k: Tactically. Behind a tactical Bram.
src: 'Tactically. Behind a tactical Bram.'

k: I _knew_ that was a real word.
src: 'I _knew_ that was a real word.'

k: Corvin Ashe. Captain of the Halcyon — finest airship in Solmere.
src: 'Corvin Ashe. Captain of the Halcyon — finest airship in Solmere.'

k: It's on the ground.
src: 'It\'s on the ground.'

k: Temporarily. We had a navigational disagreement with a sandstorm. The sandstorm won on points.
src: 'Temporarily. We had a navigational disagreement with a sandstorm. The sandstorm won on points.'

k: ...Dawnguard red. Hm.
src: '...Dawnguard red. Hm.'

k: Squire. Was. Am. ...Sort of.
src: 'Squire. Was. Am. ...Sort of.'

k: Relax, big lad. I deserted them too. Not that I'm saying you deserted. Or that I did. Hypothetically.
src: 'Relax, big lad. I deserted them too. Not that I\'m saying you deserted. Or that I did. Hypothetically.'

k: His eyes catch on the case at Wren's hip — on the Choir's gold sunburst — and stay there a moment too long.
src: 'His eyes catch on the case at Wren\'s hip — on the Choir\'s gold sunburst — and stay there a moment too long.'

k: That's Cassian's seal.
src: 'That\'s Cassian\'s seal.'

k: Tuning forks. For the Keepers. The Hierophant asked us to carry them.
src: 'Tuning forks. For the Keepers. The Hierophant asked us to carry them.'

k: Cassian's errand-runners. Small world.
src: 'Cassian\'s errand-runners. Small world.'

k: I owe that man my life, you know. Don't tell him I said so. He'd want it back.
src: 'I owe that man my life, you know. Don\'t tell him I said so. He\'d want it back.'

k: Where are you headed? Saltglass? Funny — that's exactly where I need to be. My girl needs lift-glass, and I need someone to walk between me and the next thing with teeth.
src: 'Where are you headed? Saltglass? Funny — that\'s exactly where I need to be. My girl needs lift-glass, and I need someone to walk between me and the next thing with teeth.'

k: How do you feel about escorting a charming, handsome, _financially embarrassed_ captain across the dunes?
src: 'How do you feel about escorting a charming, handsome, _financially embarrassed_ captain across the dunes?'

k: He shot a sand wyrm for us.
src: 'He shot a sand wyrm for us.'

k: _At_ a sand wyrm. Near it. In its general direction.
src: '_At_ a sand wyrm. Near it. In its general direction.'

k: He's got a gun. I like him.
src: 'He\'s got a gun. I like him.'

k: ...Three things. One: if he steals anything, he walks. Two: if he gets us killed, he walks. Three—
src: '...Three things. One: if he steals anything, he walks. Two: if he gets us killed, he walks. Three—'

k: If I'm charming, I stay? I accept your terms.
src: 'If I\'m charming, I stay? I accept your terms.'

k: We found a crashed airship called the Halcyon, and a sand wyrm trying to eat it, and a sky-pirate called Corvin Ashe trying very hard not to be eaten. He says he owes the Hierophant his life. He's coming with us to Saltglass. Ilse has rules.
src: 'We found a crashed airship called the Halcyon, and a sand wyrm trying to eat it, and a sky-pirate called Corvin Ashe trying very hard not to be eaten. He says he owes the Hierophant his life. He\'s coming with us to Saltglass. Ilse has rules.'

k: Three shards of saltglass sit in the brass housing, humming quietly to themselves. The Halcyon is dreaming of the sky.
src: 'Three shards of saltglass sit in the brass housing, humming quietly to themselves. The Halcyon is dreaming of the sky.'

k: Three good pieces of singing glass, sparrow. Then she'll remember how to float.
src: 'Three good pieces of singing glass, sparrow. Then she\'ll remember how to float.'

k: Well. Would you look at that.
src: 'Well. Would you look at that.'

k: Corvin fits the shards into the brass housing one by one, the way a man sets the table for guests he'd stopped expecting.
src: 'Corvin fits the shards into the brass housing one by one, the way a man sets the table for guests he\'d stopped expecting.'

k: The glass sings — a low, clean note you feel in your teeth. The deck shivers.
src: 'The glass sings — a low, clean note you feel in your teeth. The deck shivers.'

k: For one long breath, the Halcyon lifts a finger's width off the sand.
src: 'For one long breath, the Halcyon lifts a finger\'s width off the sand.'

k: ...And settles back with a groan.
src: '...And settles back with a groan.'
